body:
<!-- issue-pr-review-20261002 -->
## Issue/PR review — October 2, 2026

**Partially implemented; keep open.** Authenticated, independent Explorer-source results and regressions entered main in [commit f04f7ebef3bc247867ad5e4d943b6e69e5dd8876](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/commit/f04f7ebef3bc247867ad5e4d943b6e69e5dd8876); GitHub reports no associated PR for that commit. [PR #16](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/pull/16) and [PR #24](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/pull/24) are PostgreSQL/worker follow-ups, not the original implementation.

Current source includes bearer-token forwarding, separate source failures, stale-cache handling and session-storage migration tests in [tests/unit/lichess-explorer-regressions.test.ts](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/5dd0815b4bac42dea3077959fd92f1db33f4cf04/tests/unit/lichess-explorer-regressions.test.ts). Closure still requires this issue's real-service/OAuth verification and acceptance reconciliation. Also review #6: the PostgreSQL token handoff writes a 24-hour Redis key, while Compose enables append-only persistence; that does not establish the required no-durable-token guarantee. No real credentials or live services were exercised by this audit.

Reviewed against main `5dd0815b4bac42dea3077959fd92f1db33f4cf04`, all pre-existing open PRs, and merged PRs from September 18–October 2. Issue state is unchanged by this audit.

<!-- /issue-pr-review-20261002 -->

## Summary

Tempo's Builder currently shows generic **Error** state for both the Lichess player database and Masters database, and neither source is populating.

Investigation of the current implementation points to a concrete primary bug plus an observability/design problem:

1. **Tempo completes a Lichess PKCE OAuth flow and obtains an access token, but the actual requests to `explorer.lichess.org` do not send that token.**
2. Lichess changed Opening Explorer access in 2026 so Explorer requests require authenticated access.
3. The current Explorer client collapses nearly every failure into `upstream-failure`, and Builder collapses that further into a generic `error` state.
4. The Lichess and Masters requests are coupled through `Promise.all()`, so one upstream source failing makes both appear broken.
5. There have also been genuine recent Lichess Explorer / Masters availability incidents, making it important that Tempo distinguish authentication failures from rate limits, outages, malformed responses, and partial availability.

This issue should fix the authentication path **and** make future Explorer failures actionable enough that we do not need source-code archaeology to determine whether Tempo, authentication, or Lichess is failing.

I recommend keeping this as **one issue rather than splitting it into sub-issues** because the authentication fix, error model, independent-source behavior, and UI diagnostics all touch the same small Explorer boundary and need to be tested together. Do not turn this into a broad Builder refactor.

---

## Current implementation

### Explorer requests

The current client is:

`app/lib/lichess-explorer.ts`

It currently calls:

```ts
const base = "https://explorer.lichess.org";

const request = Promise.all([
  fetch(
    `${base}/lichess?variant=standard&speeds=${speeds}&ratings=${ratings}&fen=${encodeURIComponent(fen)}`,
  ),
  fetch(
    `${base}/masters?variant=standard&fen=${encodeURIComponent(fen)}`,
  ),
])
```

No `Authorization` header is sent.

`loadExplorer()` does not currently accept an access token.

### OAuth

`app/views/analysis_view.tsx` already contains a PKCE OAuth flow and exchanges the authorization code at:

```text
https://lichess.org/api/token
```

On success it currently does approximately:

```ts
localStorage.setItem("tempo-lichess-token", data.access_token);
setLichessToken(data.access_token);
```

So the current data flow is effectively:

```text
Builder
  ↓
Lichess OAuth
  ↓
access token obtained
  ↓
token stored in React state / browser storage

                     X  token never reaches request
                     ↓
Tempo → explorer.lichess.org/lichess
Tempo → explorer.lichess.org/masters
       anonymous fetches
```

This is the leading explanation for the current persistent failure.

---

## External/API context

Lichess changed Opening Explorer access in 2026 so Explorer access requires authentication. This appears to have been introduced as part of anti-abuse / DDoS mitigation.

Relevant official/current resources to verify before implementation:

- Lichess API documentation:
  https://lichess.org/api
- Lichess API specification repository:
  https://github.com/lichess-org/api
- Lichess changelog:
  https://lichess.org/page/changelog
- Opening Explorer host:
  https://explorer.lichess.org

The relevant Explorer endpoint families are:

```text
/lichess
/masters
/player
```

Before coding, verify the current authentication requirement and exact supported authorization mechanism against the current official Lichess documentation/specification. Do not rely solely on this issue if the API contract has changed again.

There have also been recent community reports of:

- Explorer suddenly failing in previously working clients after access changes;
- HTTP 502/504 Explorer outages;
- Masters database availability incidents.

Therefore, fixing the missing auth header is necessary but **not sufficient** for a robust product experience. Tempo needs to expose what actually failed.

---

## Primary fix: authenticated Explorer requests

Update the Explorer client so authenticated requests use the OAuth token.

Conceptually:

```ts
export function loadExplorer(
  fen: string,
  speeds: string,
  ratings: string,
  accessToken: string,
): Promise<...> {
  const headers = {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
  };

  // send headers to both Explorer endpoints
}
```

Do not blindly copy this exact signature if a cleaner typed request object fits the current code better.

Requirements:

- The Lichess database request receives the bearer token.
- The Masters database request receives the bearer token if the current API requires/supports it.
- Builder should not repeatedly issue known-unauthenticated requests when authentication is required.
- Completing OAuth should trigger an Explorer retry without requiring navigation/reload.
- Token values must never appear in:
  - logs;
  - diagnostics;
  - errors;
  - debug bundles;
  - rendered UI;
  - cache keys.

---

## Token storage

The README currently describes the access token as being kept in session storage, while the implementation uses `localStorage`.

Review the intended security/usability contract.

Prefer `sessionStorage` if that remains the documented product decision, so closing the browser session clears the credential.

If changing storage:

- migrate/clear the old `tempo-lichess-token` local-storage behavior safely;
- do not strand an old token in persistent storage;
- ensure OAuth completion and subsequent Builder requests still work;
- update documentation to match implementation.

Do not add refresh-token machinery unless the Lichess flow actually requires it and the current API supports it.

---

## Error handling problem

The current client effectively does:

```ts
if (lichess.status === 429 || masters.status === 429)
  throw new Error("rate-limited");

if (!lichess.ok || !masters.ok)
  throw new Error("upstream-failure");
```

Then Builder reduces most errors to:

```ts
setExplorerState("error");
```

This means all of these can become the same visible **Error**:

```text
missing authentication
401 Unauthorized
403 Forbidden
429 rate limit
500 upstream error
502 upstream outage
503 upstream outage
504 timeout
browser/network failure
CORS failure
invalid JSON
schema mismatch
Lichess database down
Masters database down
```

That is not sufficient.

---

## Introduce an explicit Explorer error/result contract

Create the smallest typed model necessary to preserve:

- source: `lichess` or `masters`;
- HTTP status when available;
- broad failure category;
- safe actionable message;
- whether cached data is available;
- whether retry is appropriate.

For example, categories might include:

```text
authentication-required
authentication-failed
rate-limited
offline
upstream-unavailable
invalid-response
network-error
```

The exact enum/model is up to the implementation.

Do not expose raw response bodies to the normal UI.

Safe technical detail such as:

```text
Masters Explorer unavailable (HTTP 504)
```

is useful.

An OAuth token is not.

---

## Decouple Lichess and Masters availability

The current `Promise.all()` architecture unnecessarily gives both sources one fate.

Desired behavior:

```text
Lichess database: Ready
Masters database: HTTP 503 / unavailable
```

should still allow Tempo to display and use the Lichess results.

Likewise:

```text
Lichess database: rate limited
Masters database: Ready
```

should retain Masters results if the upstream API permits that state.

Do not throw away successful source data because the other request failed.

Possible implementation approaches include:

- `Promise.allSettled()`;
- independent source loaders;
- a combined loader returning two independent typed results.

Choose the simplest implementation consistent with the existing domain boundaries.

---

## State model

The current single `explorerState` is probably too coarse once partial success is supported.

Prefer source-specific states conceptually like:

```text
lichessExplorerState
mastersExplorerState
```

or a structured equivalent:

```ts
{
  lichess: { state, moves, error? },
  masters: { state, moves, error? }
}
```

Do not duplicate unrelated Builder state.

The UI should be able to distinguish at least:

- off;
- loading;
- ready;
- stale;
- authentication required;
- rate limited;
- offline;
- unavailable/error.

---

## Cached-data behavior

The existing 24-hour Explorer cache is useful and should remain.

Current cache key:

```ts
fen | speeds | ratings
```

Do **not** add the OAuth token to the cache key. Explorer results are not user-private merely because access requires authentication.

Desired stale behavior:

```text
fresh request succeeds
→ update cache
→ ready

fresh request fails + valid cached result exists
→ continue showing cached result
→ mark that source stale
→ retain diagnostic about fresh-request failure

fresh request fails + no cache
→ show actionable source-specific failure
```

A failed/authentication response must never overwrite a valid cached payload.

If the two sources are independently degradable, consider whether the cache representation should also allow one source to refresh while the other retains stale data.

Keep this simple; correctness matters more than cache cleverness.

---

## UI requirements

The Builder should no longer display only generic `Error`.

Examples of acceptable user-facing states:

```text
Lichess · Sign in required
Masters · Sign in required
```

```text
Lichess · Ready
Masters · Temporarily unavailable (HTTP 504)
```

```text
Lichess · Cached · fresh request rate limited
Masters · Ready
```

```text
Lichess · Offline · showing cached data
Masters · Offline · showing cached data
```

Exact wording should fit the existing Builder UI.

Keep it compact. Do not build a large diagnostic panel inside Builder.

If an existing service-status/debug facility is appropriate for deeper detail, feed safe structured information into it rather than inventing another debugging framework.

---

## Authentication UX

If Explorer is enabled but no valid token is available:

- do not continuously hammer the endpoint anonymously;
- show that authentication is required;
- provide/use the existing Lichess connection action;
- after successful OAuth, automatically retry the current position.

If a request returns 401/403:

- distinguish this from an upstream outage;
- treat the credential as invalid/expired as appropriate;
- make reconnection possible;
- do not silently loop retries with the same bad credential.

Verify exact 401 vs 403 semantics against current Lichess behavior before encoding assumptions.

---

## Schema validation

Tempo already validates Explorer payloads through:

`explorerResponseSchema`

Keep strict validation.

A successful HTTP 200 with an incompatible payload should be classified separately from an HTTP/network failure.

Conceptually:

```text
HTTP 200
  ↓
JSON parse
  ↓
Zod/domain validation
  ↓
ready
```

If JSON/schema validation fails:

```text
invalid-response
```

Do not silently treat malformed upstream data as an empty move list.

---

## Suggested implementation locations

Primary files:

- `app/lib/lichess-explorer.ts`
- `app/views/analysis_view.tsx`
- `app/domain/schemas/index.ts` if transport/result schemas change
- relevant Explorer/Builder domain types
- relevant Builder comparison/status components
- README/docs describing token storage/authentication
- existing Explorer/Builder tests
- `tests/REGRESSIONS.md`

Potentially inspect:

- `app/components/move-comparison-table.tsx`
- service-status/debug components
- settings/authentication UI

Do not modify backend Explorer coverage machinery unless investigation shows it has the same authentication defect and needs the same repair. If it does, reuse a coherent authentication policy rather than creating contradictory browser/backend behavior.

---

## Important: inspect the backend coverage path too

Tempo also has backend code that calls Lichess Explorer for repertoire coverage.

Relevant code includes:

- `backend/app/services/repertoire_coverage.py`
- analysis capability metadata referring to `https://explorer.lichess.org/lichess`

Determine whether those backend requests are:

- currently authenticated;
- still succeeding;
- using a different endpoint/access policy;
- failing independently.

If backend coverage also needs authentication, do not silently fix only Builder and leave background coverage broken.

However, avoid unnecessarily moving the entire Builder Explorer flow through the backend unless there is a concrete reason. The current browser OAuth architecture may remain appropriate.

Document what you find.

---

## Regression coverage

Per Tempo project policy, add named regression tests and update `tests/REGRESSIONS.md`.

At minimum cover:

### 1. Authenticated request

Given a token, both Explorer requests include the expected authorization mechanism and successful payloads populate the respective move lists.

### 2. No token

When authentication is required and no token exists:

- no pointless anonymous request loop;
- UI reports sign-in/authentication required.

### 3. OAuth completion retries

After successful OAuth token acquisition, the current Builder position retries automatically and can become ready without manual navigation.

### 4. Invalid/expired credential

401/403 is surfaced as an authentication problem rather than generic upstream failure.

### 5. Rate limit

429 produces a rate-limit state.

If cached data exists, retain it as stale.

### 6. Independent failure: Masters down

Lichess succeeds and Masters returns e.g. 503/504:

- Lichess data remains visible;
- Masters reports unavailable;
- successful Lichess data is not discarded.

### 7. Independent failure: Lichess down

Masters succeeds while Lichess fails:

- Masters data remains visible;
- Lichess reports its failure.

### 8. Offline/network failure

Network failure is distinguishable from authentication/upstream HTTP failure.

Cached data remains usable when available.

### 9. Invalid payload

HTTP 200 with malformed/incompatible JSON:

- does not become an empty successful result;
- is reported as invalid upstream response;
- valid cache is preserved.

### 10. Token secrecy

Ensure diagnostics/debug state do not contain the bearer token.

### 11. Cache behavior

- successful response caches;
- failed response does not poison cache;
- stale cache remains available during upstream failure.

### 12. Token storage contract

If moving to `sessionStorage`, cover the new behavior and removal/migration of persistent local-storage token state.

---

## Manual verification

After implementation, verify against the real Lichess service, not only mocked tests.

From Builder:

1. Start from the initial position.
2. Authenticate with Lichess if required.
3. Confirm Lichess database results populate.
4. Confirm Masters database results populate.
5. Navigate several positions.
6. Confirm requests continue succeeding.
7. Reload/reopen according to the chosen token-storage semantics.
8. Confirm failure states are understandable if authentication is removed/invalidated.

Use browser network tooling during manual verification and record:

- endpoint;
- HTTP status;
- whether Authorization was sent;
- safe error category.

Never record the token value.

---

## Research/verification before closing

Check the current official Lichess API documentation/specification and confirm:

- whether both `/lichess` and `/masters` require bearer authentication;
- whether OAuth tokens with no scopes are sufficient;
- relevant rate-limit behavior;
- whether any request parameter behavior has changed;
- whether direct browser requests are supported as currently implemented.

If current docs contradict assumptions in this issue, follow the official API contract and document the difference in the implementation summary.

---

## Definition of done

This issue is complete when:

> Builder can authenticate to the current Lichess Opening Explorer API and populate both the Lichess and Masters datasets when they are available. If one source, authentication, the network, rate limits, or upstream validation fails, Tempo preserves any usable source/cache data and tells the user what actually failed instead of showing only generic Error.

Additionally:

- the OAuth token actually reaches requests that require it;
- successful sources survive failure of the other source;
- token storage matches documented behavior;
- tokens never leak into diagnostics;
- cached results degrade gracefully;
- backend coverage Explorer usage has been checked for the same auth issue;
- regression coverage is recorded in `tests/REGRESSIONS.md`.

---

## Out of scope

Do not expand this into:

- general Builder architecture refactor;
- replacement of Lichess Explorer;
- local mirror of Lichess databases;
- new analytics database;
- OAuth framework abstraction for hypothetical future providers;
- broad service-status redesign;
- unrelated repertoire coverage changes.

Fix the Explorer boundary comprehensively but narrowly.

---

## Expected implementation report

When complete, report:

1. Root cause confirmed from actual HTTP behavior/current docs.
2. Files changed.
3. Authentication mechanism used.
4. Token-storage decision.
5. New source-specific state/error model.
6. Partial-failure behavior.
7. Backend coverage-path findings.
8. Tests added and commands run.
9. Manual real-service verification results.
10. Any remaining upstream Lichess limitation Tempo cannot control.
title: Repair Lichess Opening Explorer authentication, independent source failures, and diagnostics
